title: Hannibal: the person and the accounts that remain
purpose: Preserve a walkable path from a famous historical-person label back to bounded surviving source reports while keeping mediation, source dependence and unknowns visible.

subject.identity_ceiling: The entity is a thin routing anchor. Source-literal mentions remain separately inspectable and candidate-linked; the record does not turn the surviving biography into the person.

selection.selected_for: Historical-person source-survival and source-dependence stress case after the first three public records tested artwork provenance, repeated-claim ancestry and living-practice transmission.
selection.boundary: Selection did not establish representativeness, historical priority, importance or entitlement. Publication followed bounded source/reader review and current-validator compatibility checks; reader benefit remains unestablished.
selection.selection_history_ceiling: No selection-time candidate pool or alternatives list is preserved from the pre-publication selection process; do not reconstruct one after the fact.

notes: Thin routing anchor for the historical human conventionally called Hannibal Barca; exact dates, appearance, routes and biographical details are not identity-key material.

The checked Nepos Latin passage attests the literal string 'Hannibal'. The checked Polybius reading surface renders the name as 'Hannibal' in English; this record did not inspect the Greek source literal. The fuller modern display label is conventional rather than claimed as source-attested by both checked surfaces.
Two public source-literal mentions remain candidate-linked rather than silently upgraded into identity certainty.

sources.title: Dickinson College Commentaries: Nepos, Life of Hannibal, chapter 13

observations.scope: Chapter 13, especially Latin paragraph 13.3 and its commentary on Silenus and Sosylus; not manuscript evidence or a complete audit of DCC.
notes: Ancient text and modern editorial commentary are separate evidential layers.

sources.title: Polybius, Histories Book 3 — LacusCurtius/Thayer
sources.publisher: LacusCurtius / University of Chicago-hosted reading surface

observations.scope: Book 3 passages 3.20.5, 3.33.17-18, 3.48.12 and 3.56.3-4 on source criticism, the Lacinium tablet, Alpine inquiry/inspection and force totals; not a full-book critical edition review.
notes: This is a modern web reading surface for an ancient text, not the ancient carrier.
The host presents the English text as the 1922 Loeb translation and warns that the web page has not yet been proofread; this fixture does not treat it as a checked critical edition.

mentions.context: Nepos, Hannibal 13.3, sentence identifying Sosylus as Hannibal's Greek teacher.

basis: The source is Nepos' Life of Hannibal chapter 13 and the literal occurs inside that named subject context; linked only as a candidate to the conventional modern Hannibal Barca anchor, not as identity proof.

mentions.context: Polybius, Histories 3.33.17-18 on the checked 1922 Loeb English reading surface, where Paton's translation renders the narrative subject as 'Hannibal'.

basis: The checked English reading surface at Polybius 3.33.17-18 renders the campaign subject as 'Hannibal'; linked only as a candidate to the conventional modern Hannibal Barca anchor, not as independent identity proof. The Greek source literal was not inspected in this record.

scope.ceiling: Nepos reports that Silenus and Sosylus were with Hannibal and wrote about the war; THR has not inspected their complete works.

object.literal: Polybius dismisses the authority of Sosylus and Chaereas.

scope.ceiling: This is Polybius' evaluation of another historian, not THR's adjudication of Sosylus.

object.literal: A bronze tablet at the Lacinian promontory carrying Hannibal's troop lists.

scope.ceiling: Polybius reports finding and using the bronze tablet described at 3.33.17-18. THR has not observed that ancient carrier or an independently preserved copy, and this fixture does not establish that it is physically identical to the column/inscription described at 3.56.4.

subject.literal: Polybius' claimed investigation of the Alpine crossing

object.literal: Polybius says he questioned men who had been present, inspected the country, and crossed the Alps himself.

scope.ceiling: This records Polybius' own account of his evidence-gathering method. THR did not observe the reported interviews, route inspection, travel, or ancient investigation.

object.literal: Hannibal crossed the Alps into Italy.

scope.ceiling: Attribution to Polybius' surviving account; exact pass and complete source ancestry are not established by this fixture.

current_findings: Two bounded ancient-text reading surfaces make attributed reports about Hannibal and their own source world inspectable.
Polybius' reports about a Lacinium tablet and his own investigative method remain reports by Polybius, not direct THR observations.
Nepos attests Silenus and Sosylus as companions/historians; their complete works are not represented as inspected THR source objects.
The checked aperture is asymmetric and incomplete; later repetition is not counted as independent corroboration by default.
Stable classical-text edition identifiers can be added as record-local recovery routes without treating a catalogue identity as manuscript verification or changing any historical assertion.
unknowns: A complete source genealogy among Polybius, Livy and other surviving writers.
The full Punic/Carthaginian documentary aperture and all surviving fragments.
Whether the Lacinium tablet described at 3.33 and column/inscription at 3.56 are the same physical carrier.
The exact Alpine pass and many other biographical/historical disputes outside this record.

Manuscript-level verification remains unperformed. DCC declares a Rolfe 1929 textual basis with editorial modifications, but THR has not line-by-line collated chapter 13 against that print edition; a stable Perseus Greek Polybius edition route is identified, but THR has not established it as the textual basis of the Paton/Loeb reading surface or newly inspected the Greek source-language passages.

inspection_boundary.lacinium_carrier_identity: The relationship or physical identity between the bronze tablet described at 3.33.17-18 and the column/inscription described at 3.56.4 is not established by this fixture.
inspection_boundary.edition_identity: DCC textual-basis metadata and Perseus CTS edition identities inspected; no manuscript collation, no line-by-line DCC-to-Rolfe collation, and no claim that the Perseus Greek Polybius edition underlies Paton's English translation.

strongest_owner: Classical source criticism, critical editions and specialist ancient-history scholarship own historical reconstruction. THR adds only a cross-record public evidence route and correction surface.

rights_and_custody.project_record: Project-authored record material is governed by the repository's stated CC0 scope only to the extent the project holds those rights.
rights_and_custody.third_party_sources: Linked ancient-text/editorial/scholarly source surfaces retain their own rights and custody; THR does not re-license them.
rights_and_custody.subject_liveness: Historical deceased subject; this record makes no claim about descendants, communities or cultural authority beyond the cited public evidence.

correction_rule.rule: Material corrections should identify the affected proposition/source, preserve the prior repository state, state what was checked and distinguish fresh evidence from reinterpretation.

edition_routes.basis: Dickinson College Commentaries credits state that its Latin Prologue and Life of Hannibal are based on J. C. Rolfe's 1929 Loeb edition, with punctuation changes and specified textual alterations.
